coverage_warning: No critique, rebuttal, failed replication or retraction turned up this week, so this issue shows no pushback on any claim; PubPeer and arXiv "Comment on" listings were not checked.

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: The Galileo Project plans a roughly $1.5M radar-plus-telescope observatory in Ithaca, New York, to track and identify aerial objects.
cards.people: Avi Loeb (Harvard; described as chair of the UAP Science Advisory Council); backer Adam Weitsman (entrepreneur, affiliation not in source)
cards.stage_note: This is an announced observatory, not a result. A Nov 5 announcement said work would start this month and finish in about a year; no discoveries have been claimed.
cards.impact_heading: IF IT WORKS, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: It would be the project's fourth observatory and its first to combine continuous radar with a large optical telescope. Calibrated, multi-sensor data is what the UAP field lacks.

details.heading: What the plan says
details.text: Radar would find targets and point a 0.7 m PlaneWave CDK700 telescope at them, with AI support and spectra. Readings would be checked against known flight activity. The site is a property once owned by Carl Sagan.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: The headline's "prove UFOs are foreign black projects" framing is not supported by the article, which treats that only as a hypothesis to investigate.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: Published calibration, a false-positive rate measured against known aircraft and satellites, and open data.

cards.todo: No action now. Watch for a commissioning or instrument paper.
cards.rule_text: A first commissioning or instrument paper with radar–optical cross-matching appears; only then consider supporting an independent data audit.

cards.label: PENDING
cards.meta: MOND / MODIFIED GRAVITY · ZENODO CODE PACKAGE · NOV 15
cards.claim: A code package fits dark matter halos and six modified-gravity models to both the Milky Way's rotation curve and its vertical gravity.
cards.people: Robert Monjo (CUNEF University; Universidad de Chile); A. E. Sasi (affiliation not in source); paper listed as "in preparation"
cards.stage_headline: Not rated yet: only code and method seen.
cards.stage_note: Only the software (version 2.0.0) and method description exist. The accompanying paper isn't out, so the results are unknown.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: Requiring one model to fit both the radial and the vertical gravity is a harder test than fitting a rotation curve alone.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: The planned method: NFW and Einasto halos, QUMOND, STVG, Verlinde's emergent gravity, f(R), refracted gravity and hyperconical modified gravity (HMG), fitted to 152 model-independent rotation-curve points and 44 vertical-potential measurements from Wang et al. (2026). Four sets of 100 random baryonic-mass draws, compared by BIC; QUMOND, STVG and refracted gravity solved with full field equations.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Which model wins; how much the baryonic-mass assumptions drive the answer; whether either author developed one of the models tested (not stated in the source).

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: The paper shared publicly with the full ranking, the result holding across all four baryonic sets, and someone outside the group rerunning the code.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: If HMG or another niche model wins only under one baryonic set, the result is fragile. If MOND-type models fit the radial data but fail the vertical data, that counts against them.

cards.todo: Wait for the paper; when it appears, have a reviewer rerun the 29.2 MB package before any contact.
cards.rule_text: The paper appears on arXiv with a BIC table.
cards.compare_text: Recent wide-binary tests report no MOND signal, including forward modelling of 3D orbits (arXiv 2603.11015) and high-precision C3PO radial velocities (arXiv 2512.19652).

compare_link.label: arXiv: A Quality Framework for Testing Gravity with Wide Binaries: No Evidence for MOND ↗

cards.label: PENDING
cards.claim: A new galaxy study is said to support CCC+TL, a cosmology with no dark matter or dark energy and a universe 26.7 billion years old.
cards.people: Rajendra Gupta (adjunct professor of physics, University of Ottawa) and a postdoctoral researcher (name not in source)
cards.stage_headline: Not rated yet: we only saw a press release.
cards.stage_note: The full page wouldn't load; details come from the search excerpt. Paper title, venue and DOI not seen.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: It would remove dark matter and dark energy, but the model's age for the universe is about twice the standard value.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: The release says the galaxy study is one of a series of CCC+TL tests run in 2025–26. What was tested and how well it fits are unknown.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: Matching the cosmic microwave background power spectrum, Big Bang element abundances and the ages of the oldest stars at the same time, not one dataset at a time.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: A clear conflict with the microwave background or with stellar ages. A reader comment says galaxy sizes conflict with the model, but that is not a published critique.

cards.rule_text: Revisit only if the underlying paper is peer-reviewed and tests the microwave background.
cards.compare_text: Planck 2018 cosmological parameters give an age of about 13.8 billion years.

primary_link.label: SciTechDaily: A universe without dark matter ↗

cards.label: PENDING
cards.meta: VACUUM / DARK ENERGY · PRESS RELEASE · NOV 13
cards.claim: A reading of DESI data allows two cosmic histories, one in which effective dark energy had negative density in the distant past, depending on today's matter density.
cards.stage_headline: Not rated yet: we only saw a press release.
cards.stage_note: The paper has not been seen. The release itself says the findings "do not yet establish that dark energy changes over time."
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: As context: a dark energy that changes over time would change the mainstream picture that vacuum-energy claims are judged against.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: The paper, its authors and whether DESI's own collaboration analyses support the reading.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: The release's own caveat: the result does not establish evolving dark energy.

cards.todo: Identify the paper; until then keep constant dark energy (Λ) as the benchmark for vacuum claims.
cards.rule_text: The paper is identified and DESI's own collaboration analyses support a dark energy that changes over time.
cards.compare_text: Constant dark energy (Λ) remains the benchmark for vacuum-energy claims.

cards.label: CONTEXT
cards.claim: Out-of-body and other unusual bodily experiences come with brain activity that mixes features of sleep and waking.
cards.people: Teresa Campillo-Ferrer (Radboud University) and colleagues, Consciousness and Cognition
cards.stage_headline: Stage 3 of 5: tested against a control.
cards.stage_note: Based on news coverage: recordings during reported experiences were compared with participants' own sleep and meditation recordings. No independent replication or preregistration reported; the paper predates the window (exact date unconfirmed).
cards.impact_text: It offers an ordinary brain mechanism that any claim of accurate perception during out-of-body experiences has to rule out.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: 35 participants wore EEG caps; 20 reported 36 experiences, 10 involving being outside or above the body, marked with a set left-right eye-movement signal. Delta and theta dropped and beta and gamma rose, mainly over the temporal lobes.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Whether the whole brain was in an in-between state or different regions were asleep and awake at once.

details.heading: Would weaken it
details.text: The same EEG pattern showing up equally often without any reported experience.

cards.todo: Read the paper and file it as the comparison point for any out-of-body-experience proposal; a July 2026 bioRxiv preprint on brain-signal complexity during these experiences was seen in search but not opened.
cards.rule_text: Any OBE or veridical-perception proposal we consider must address this sleep–wake mixing mechanism.

cards.label: BENCHMARK
cards.claim: Euclid has found about 15,000 candidate strong gravitational lenses in a single, uniformly analysed catalogue, more than all earlier collections combined.
cards.people: UBC researchers including Srivastava (first name not in source)
cards.stage_headline: Stage 2 of 5: uses data, but no comparison group.
cards.stage_note: These are observed candidates, not yet confirmed lenses. The page wouldn't load and the catalogue paper is not yet identified.
cards.impact_text: Any MOND-type theory has to explain lensing without dark matter; a large uniform catalogue makes it much harder to pick only the systems that suit a theory.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: The catalogue paper, confirmation rates and the analysis details.

cards.todo: Find the catalogue paper next week.
cards.rule_text: Any MOND or emergent-gravity proposal we consider must say how it handles strong lensing statistics.
